meta.name: Tokyo (the centre and the bay)
meta.scaleNote: game units per real metre; uniform, no compression
meta.originNote: Shimbashi / Shiodome: the east side of Shimbashi Station by the Nittele Tower
meta.coverage: North edge past Otemachi, the Bank of Japan and the Imperial Palace East Gardens; south to the Rainbow Bridge, Takanawa Gateway and the north tip of Odaiba (Fuji TV); west past Akasaka, Roppongi 1-chome and Mita; east over the Sumida mouth to Tsukuda, Harumi and the Toyosu wharf. 887 x 1431 u (4.4 x 7.2 km).
meta.terrain: FLAT. Central Tokyo's relief is modest (the Yamanote plateau at Atago, Azabudai, Nagatacho and Takanawa stands 20-30 m over the reclaimed low city); the game ground is flat and the hills are not modelled. Heights are measured from each building's own ground. Road tunnels and underpasses that duplicate a surface street are left out; the Shuto Expressway's tunnels are kept (tunnel: true).
meta.axes: +X = east, -Z = north (true north up), +Y up. Matches the minimap (screen up = -Z).
meta.gridNote: Central Tokyo has no single street grid: the castle-town blocks of each quarter turn with the moats, the old shoreline and the hills, so every building and landmark carries its own real rot. The largest regular grid is Ginza / Kyobashi / Nihonbashi's: Chuo-dori and the streets parallel to it bear about 42 deg (north-east), the cross streets (Harumi-dori) about 132 deg; street-aligned rot about -0.73. Marunouchi and Otemachi turn about 15 deg west of north (rot about -0.26), Tsukishima / Kachidoki / Harumi lie at 40 deg like Ginza, Shibaura and Takeshiba follow the quays. Landmark front = compass point of frontBearing (deg clockwise from north) and frontDir = the world (x, z) unit vector; grid = 'ginza' where the footprint sits on the Ginza grid, else 'local'. Japan drives on the left; that is not modelled.
meta.rotNote: All rot values are three.js rotation.y (radians). An object rotated by rot has its local +X axis pointing along (cos rot, -sin rot) in world (x, z). Building w is along local X, d along local Z: footprints are oriented rects (OBB), not axis-aligned. rot is folded into (-pi/4, pi/4], except landmarks of kind bridge (kachidoki_bridge, nihonbashi_bridge, rainbow_bridge), whose w is the deck length and rot the deck direction.
meta.footprintNote: Footprints are CCW viewed from above (CCW in (x, -z)), open rings (first vertex not repeated). For THREE.Shape use (x, -z) then rotateX(-PI/2).
meta.heightNote: height / eaveHeight are game units (metres x 0.2). Landmarks: heightMetres = top of the structure incl. spires and masts; eaveMetres = main roof, or where the crown / spire begins; dataRoofMetres = the OSM height of the matched footprint. Buildings: heightMetres = the OpenStreetMap height tag, else the height of the tallest building:part, else building:levels x 3.4 (3.9 from 20 floors) + 1.5; where OSM gives none (most of the small lots) a zone-typical height by footprint area (the core's pencil buildings 17-33 m, the low city's houses 7-12 m) averaged with the median of the mapped heights of similar-sized neighbours within 150 m, +-18% by a hash of the id; a merged block mass takes the area-weighted height and keeps heightMaxMetres.
meta.mergeNote: Touching or nearly touching buildings (2.5 m) under 60 m within 2x of each other in height are merged while their union fills at least 56% of its rectangle and no side passes 120 m; lots under 1,600 m2 then fold into the nearest-height neighbour (3.5x, fill 38%), and last the rows either side of a dropped back alley (gap up to 5.5 m) join into block masses, never across a street that is kept in roads. Tokyo's rows of 4-8 m wide pencil buildings and wooden houses become block-face masses this way. A tower standing on a podium in the data (building:part) is split into the tower (its own entry) and the podium (podiumOf = the tower's id). footprint = the outline; cx/cz/w/d/rot = its oriented rectangle (what the kit fills); phoneSkip = the smallest, lowest masses away from the streets (30%: phones build about 70%).
meta.buildingFields: osm = the OpenStreetMap way / relation of the outline (the largest member of a merged row); onPier = stands on a pier deck or over the water (keep it, do not drop it as in-water); zone = marunouchi / otemachi / nihonbashi / ginza / yurakucho / shimbashi / shiodome / kasumigaseki / nagatacho / akasaka / toranomon / roppongi / shiba / hamamatsucho / takeshiba / tsukiji / tsukishima / kachidoki / harumi / toyosu / tamachi / shibaura / takanawa / odaiba / imperial_palace; style (generic only; landmark footprints carry landmark = the id and no style) = house (1-3 storey wooden / light houses and shop-houses), zakkyo (narrow 4-10 storey multi-tenant pencil buildings with signboards), apartment (mansion blocks, danchi slabs, tower-mansion podiums), lowrise (other < 15 m), midrise (15-60 m offices / ministries / hotels / department stores), warehouse (wharf sheds, markets, depots), glassslab (60-120 m), glasstower (120 m and more); frontage = avenue (on a major street) / street; merged = number of outlines in the mass.
meta.roadNote: roads are the pieces of each OSM street between junctions (name = name:en where mapped, nameJa = the Japanese name). The narrow back streets are thinned: a minor street piece is dropped while a block beside it is under 2,750 m2, so the kept minors bound the merged blocks; alleys (service / footway) are not roads. expressway: true = the Shuto Expressway (Inner Circular C1, Route 1 Haneda / Ueno, Route 2, Route 3, Route 4, Route 6, Yaesu line, Route 11 Daiba over the Rainbow Bridge), the Tokyo Expressway (KK line) and their ramps: mostly elevated (bridge: true), in cuttings round the palace moats and under Kasumigaseki / Shiodome (tunnel: true). Expressways are not in roadGraph.
meta.waterNote: water kind bay = Tokyo Bay, the port, the Sumida River, the Nihonbashi / Kamejima / Kanda rivers and the canals of Shibaura, Tsukiji, Tsukishima, Harumi and Toyosu (one tidal body from the OSM coastline plus the river and canal areas, clipped to the box, islands and wharves as holes); kind pond = inland water: the Imperial Palace moats (Sakurada-bori, Hanzo-bori, Hibiya-bori, Babasaki-bori, Kikyo-bori, Ote-bori ...), the ponds of Hibiya Park, Shiba Park, Kyu-Shiba-rikyu and the hotel gardens. The tidal pond of Hama-rikyu joins the bay. Every polygon is wet (wade-able).
meta.projection: equirectangular about origin: x = (lon-lon0)*90542.3*scale, z = -(lat-lat0)*110952.8*scale (WGS84 metres per degree at lat0)
meta.source: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright), BBBike extract of Tokyo (download.bbbike.org, snapshot 2026-11): coastline, rivers, canals and moats, piers, roads, parks, paths, bridges, rail and guideway lines, ferry routes, building outlines, names, heights, levels and building parts, mapped trees. Terrain tiles (Mapzen / AWS Open Data terrarium; SRTM / GSI) for the surround's ground heights. Landmark heights: CTBUH / Skyscraper Center and Wikipedia figures as given in tools/tokyo/SPEC.md.
meta.generator: tools/tokyo/cartographer/ (extract_osm.py, prep.py, gen_layout.py, gen_layout2.py, landmarks.py, lm_table.py, lm_info.py, zones.py, gen_detail.py, gen_surround.py, gen_trees.py, validate.py, preview.py)
meta.gridsNote: degrees WEST of north of each grid's north-south streets (negative = east of north); lots elsewhere carry their own rot
meta.gridRotationNote: degrees clockwise of north of the Ginza / Nihonbashi grid: Chuo-dori bears about 42 deg

movedLandmarks.reason: Tokyo Skytree really stands at Oshiage, Sumida ward, about 6.7 km north-east of the origin and 2.4 km outside the box; it is moved onto the open lawn plaza of Harumi Futo Park at the tip of the Harumi wharf (reclaimed land, the former passenger-terminal site), where nothing else is built.

approximatedLandmarks.note: the OSM outline (way/195551651, still named Sapporo Ginza Building) covers the whole corner block, larger than Ginza Place itself (about 25 x 30 m at the crossing corner)
the South Tower (2021, OSM height 197 m) is the mapped footprint; the 235 m main tower beside it is still a construction site in the data
the west tower (Central Government Building No. 7 West, 176 m) only; the 156 m east tower is a generic glasstower lot
the box is the 95 m leg spread centred on the main deck; FootTown (relation/4247312) lies inside it
the Fish Intermediate Wholesale building (block 6); the Fruit and Vegetable building (block 5) is east of the box
the entry is the Tsukiji Uogashi halls; the shop rows of the outer market north of it are generic house / zakkyo lots
the terminal building on the pier (way/436096961) inside the ferry-terminal area relation/2136745
River Point Tower (40 floors, 132 m) at the tip of Tsukuda; SPEC height 140
true site at Kachidoki 6-chome, about 500 m south-west of the SPEC coordinate
x / z = mid-span of the OSM expressway deck; w = the 921 m of deck between the anchorage blocks with their end spans; towers by the published 570 m main span (detail.rainbowBridge)

minimap.note: District names for the minimap (centres) and the tier-A landmarks to mark on it; the map itself draws from roads / water / parks / buildings. Screen up = -Z (north).

landmarks.name: Tokyo Tower
landmarks.desc: The 1958 broadcasting tower on the hill of Shiba Park, 333 m: an open steel lattice on four splayed legs painted in bands of international orange and white, modelled on the Eiffel Tower but lighter. The two-storey main deck sits at 150 m, the small top deck at 250 m, a slim antenna mast above. The five-storey FootTown block (grey, flat-roofed) fills the space between the legs.
landmarks.osm: relation/4247312 (FootTown) + way/313815246 (main deck; the leg spread of 95 m is the box)

landmarks.name: Tokyo Skytree
landmarks.desc: The 2012 broadcasting tower, 634 m, the tallest tower in the world: a pale blue-white ('Skytree white') steel lattice round a concrete core, triangular at the base with a 68 m side and turning to a circle by 300 m, two flared observation decks at 350 m and 450 m and a slim gain tower above. MOVED: the real tower stands at Oshiage, 6 km north-east of the map; here it rises from the open lawn of Harumi Futo Park at the tip of the Harumi wharf.
landmarks.osm: way/288269147 (true site at Oshiage; moved to Harumi Futo Park)

landmarks.name: Azabudai Hills Mori JP Tower
landmarks.desc: Pelli Clarke & Partners' 2023 tower at Azabudai Hills, 330 m, the tallest building in Japan: a softly rounded square shaft of pale glass that swells slightly and tapers to a domed, petal-like crown split by four vertical seams. It stands over Heatherwick's rolling green-roofed pergola podium in the valley west of Tokyo Tower.

landmarks.name: Toranomon Hills Mori Tower
landmarks.desc: The 2014 Mori tower built over the Loop Road No. 2 tunnel, 247 m: a blue-green glass slab with knife-edged, faceted corners and a sloped, wedge-cut crown. A lawn garden steps up over the road portal at its foot.

landmarks.name: Toranomon Hills Station Tower
landmarks.desc: OMA's 2023 tower over Toranomon Hills subway station, 266 m: a glass tower whose faces fold along a central vertical band of activity, capped by the glass box of the TOKYO NODE halls with a rooftop infinity pool. A wide pedestrian bridge crosses Sakurada-dori to the Mori Tower.

landmarks.name: Tokyo Midtown Yaesu
landmarks.desc: The 2022 Yaesu Central Tower, 240 m, facing Tokyo Station across Sotobori-dori: a clear-glass tower with gently curved corners and a sail-like curved top, a hotel in its upper floors. Its base holds a bus terminal and a primary school behind a ribbed glass podium.

landmarks.name: Tokiwabashi Tower
landmarks.desc: Tokiwabashi Tower of the Tokyo Torch district (2021, 212 m): a crisp rectangular office slab in silver-grey glass with fine vertical fins and stacked terraces cut into its lower corner, north of Tokyo Station beside the Nihonbashi River.

landmarks.name: Marunouchi Building
landmarks.desc: The 2002 rebuild of the 'Maru-Biru', 180 m: a glass office tower set back on a stone-clad five-storey podium that recalls the 1923 original, a tall three-bay arched entrance on the Gyoko-dori corner. It frames the station plaza with its near-twin across the avenue.

landmarks.name: Shin-Marunouchi Building
landmarks.desc: The 2007 Shin-Marunouchi Building, 198 m, by Michael Hopkins: a slim grey-glass tower on a seven-storey podium of cream stone, bronze and brick with a rounded crown, paired with the Marunouchi Building across Gyoko-dori.

landmarks.name: JP Tower (KITTE)
landmarks.desc: The 2012 JP Tower, 200 m: a sheer faceted glass tower rising behind the kept white-tiled modernist front of the 1931 Tokyo Central Post Office (now the KITTE mall) with its clock, on the south side of the station plaza.

landmarks.name: GranTokyo North Tower
landmarks.desc: GranTokyo North Tower (2007, 205 m), the north bookend of Tokyo Station's Yaesu side: a tall crystal-clear glass slab by Helmut Jahn over the Daimaru department store, joined to its twin by the long white sail of the GranRoof canopy.

landmarks.name: GranTokyo South Tower
landmarks.desc: GranTokyo South Tower (2007, 205 m), the south bookend of the Yaesu side: the same clear, sharp-edged glass slab as the North Tower, standing free at the end of the GranRoof canopy.

landmarks.name: Otemachi Tower
landmarks.desc: The 2014 Otemachi Tower, 200 m: a dark, sober glass office tower with a hotel in its top floors; a third of its site is the 'Otemachi Forest', a real transplanted woodland at street level.

landmarks.name: Tokyo Midtown Hibiya
landmarks.desc: The 2018 Hibiya Mitsui Tower, 192 m, facing Hibiya Park: a glass tower with softly curved, overlapping faces (the 'dancing tower') above a stone-banded podium with a stepped roof garden and a round plaza.

landmarks.name: Dentsu Building (Caretta Shiodome)
landmarks.desc: Jean Nouvel's 2002 Dentsu headquarters at Shiodome, 213 m: a razor-thin boomerang-plan blade whose ceramic-fritted glass fades from white to dark grey across the curve, with glass lifts running up the sharp north edge. The Caretta Shiodome mall is at its foot.

landmarks.name: Nittele Tower
landmarks.desc: Richard Rogers' 2003 Nippon Television tower, 193 m: a boxy glass tower hung inside four huge exposed steel mega-columns with cross-braced frames on the outside, studios in the wide base and the copper Ghibli clock on its deck.

landmarks.name: Shiodome City Center
landmarks.desc: Kevin Roche's 2003 tower, 216 m: a green-glass tower with one long convex face like a full sail and knife-edge ends, standing where Japan's first railway terminus was (the rebuilt old Shimbashi Station is at its foot).

landmarks.name: Shiodome Media Tower
landmarks.desc: The 2003 Kyodo News headquarters, 172 m: a slim tower of dark glass with a gently bowed face, a hotel in its top floors with a tall atrium slot.

landmarks.name: Tokyo Shiodome Building (Conrad)
landmarks.desc: The 2005 Tokyo Shiodome Building, 173 m, with the Conrad hotel in its top ten floors: a broad silver-grey glass slab with rounded ends looking over the Hama-rikyu Gardens.

landmarks.name: Kasumigaseki Building
landmarks.desc: Japan's first skyscraper (1968, 147 m, 36 floors): a plain rectangular slab with a tight grid of white aluminium mullions over dark glass and a flat top, on a broad paved plaza.

landmarks.name: Kasumigaseki Common Gate
landmarks.desc: The west tower of Central Government Building No. 7 (2007, 176 m): a blue-grey glass office tower with a stone-framed base, built with its east twin round the kept 1930s brick Ministry of Education front.

landmarks.name: Sanno Park Tower
landmarks.desc: The 2000 Sanno Park Tower, 194 m, beside the Prime Minister's office: a heavy symmetrical tower of grey granite and glass, the centre of each face recessed between corner piers, a flat crown with a tall mast.

landmarks.name: Izumi Garden Tower
landmarks.desc: The 2002 Izumi Garden Tower at Roppongi 1-chome, 201 m: a green-glass tower stepped back in tiers at the top, with glass lift shafts climbing its outside over a terraced hillside garden.

landmarks.name: ARK Mori Building
landmarks.desc: The 1986 centre-piece of ARK Hills, 153 m: a broad, chamfered tower of bronze-tinted glass and brown tile with a flat helipad top, on a podium with Suntory Hall's plaza behind.

landmarks.name: Atago Green Hills Mori Tower
landmarks.desc: Cesar Pelli's 2001 office tower on the Atago hill, 187 m: a pale glass shaft with rounded corners that opens at the top into a crown of four curved petals; its residential twin (the Forest Tower) stands to the south across the temple grounds.

landmarks.name: World Trade Center Building (Hamamatsucho)
landmarks.desc: The World Trade Center Building South Tower (2021) of the Hamamatsucho rebuild beside the station and the monorail terminus: a sheer rectangular tower of silver-blue glass with fine vertical fins; the main tower rising beside it replaces the dark 1970 original.

landmarks.name: Tokyo Port City Takeshiba
landmarks.desc: The 2020 Port City Takeshiba office tower, 208 m: a wide glass slab whose lower eight floors step back toward the bay as planted terraces (the 'Skip Terrace'), linked to Takeshiba pier and Hamamatsucho by a long deck.

landmarks.name: NEC Supertower
landmarks.desc: The 1990 NEC headquarters at Mita, 180 m, the 'rocket': a silver metal-and-glass tower that narrows in three stepped tiers, with a great square wind hole through the building above the atrium at the first step.

landmarks.name: St. Luke's Garden Tower
landmarks.desc: St. Luke's Garden (1994) on the Sumida at Akashicho: the 221 m office tower with a pinched, notched top and the 146 m residence tower, both in pale silver panels, joined high up by a skybridge.

landmarks.name: The Tokyo Towers (Sea Tower)
landmarks.desc: Sea Tower of The Tokyo Towers (2008, 194 m, 58 floors), the south twin at the tip of Kachidoki: a tall white-and-grey condominium tower with glass balcony bands and rounded corners over the Asashio Canal.

landmarks.name: The Tokyo Towers (Mid Tower)
landmarks.desc: Mid Tower of The Tokyo Towers (2008, 194 m, 58 floors), the north twin: identical white-and-grey condominium tower with glass balcony bands, joined to the Sea Tower by a low podium.

landmarks.name: Harumi Island Triton Square
landmarks.desc: Harumi Island Triton Square (2001): three office towers in a row along the Asashio Canal stepping up 155 / 175 / 195 m (Z, Y, X), pale grey with blue glass and rounded ends, on a shared podium of shops, a concert hall and terraced gardens.

landmarks.name: River City 21 (Century Park Tower)
landmarks.desc: Century Park Tower (1999, 180 m, 54 floors), the tallest of the River City 21 condominium towers on Tsukuda island: a slender cream-and-brown tower with a stepped, lantern-like crown.

landmarks.name: River City 21 (Skylight Tower)
landmarks.desc: River Point Tower (1989, 132 m, 40 floors) at the very tip of Tsukuda where the Sumida divides: a triangular-plan condominium tower in cream tile with rounded balconied corners, the first of River City 21's towers.

landmarks.name: The Prince Park Tower Tokyo
landmarks.desc: The 2005 Prince Park Tower Tokyo, 104 m, in Shiba Park at the foot of Tokyo Tower: a broad curved hotel slab in warm stone-coloured panels with a glazed crown, set in lawns.

landmarks.name: Fuji TV headquarters (Odaiba)
landmarks.desc: Kenzo Tange's 1996 Fuji Television headquarters on Odaiba, 123 m: two silver towers joined by an open lattice of three levels of sky corridors on giant columns, with a 32 m titanium-clad sphere (the observation room) lodged high in the frame, and a broad stair up to a seventh-floor roof plaza.

landmarks.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department
landmarks.desc: The 1980 Metropolitan Police headquarters at Sakuradamon, 84 m: a wedge-plan block in pale brown tile whose rounded prow faces the palace moat, topped by a cylindrical communications tower bristling with antennas.

landmarks.name: Tokyo Station (Marunouchi building)
landmarks.desc: Tatsuno Kingo's 1914 Marunouchi station building, restored in 2012: a 335 m red-brick front with white granite banding, three storeys under slate roofs, a gabled centre entrance for the Imperial family and an octagonal dome over each of the north and south halls. The platforms and their canopies lie behind, the GranTokyo towers beyond.

landmarks.name: National Diet Building
landmarks.desc: The 1936 National Diet: a symmetrical granite building 206 m wide, the two chambers in the wings, with a square central tower ending in a stepped pyramid 65 m high over a columned portico. It looks east down a ginkgo avenue to the palace.

landmarks.name: Nijubashi (Seimon Ishibashi) and the main gate
landmarks.desc: The Seimon Ishibashi, the double-arched stone bridge of 1887 with its iron lamps, crossing the moat to the white-walled main gate of the palace; behind it on the high stone rampart stands the two-storey Fushimi-yagura keep with its flanking galleries (extra.keep). The postcard view of the palace from Kokyo Gaien.

landmarks.name: Imperial Palace (Kyuden)
landmarks.desc: The 1968 Imperial Palace: long, low steel-and-concrete halls in traditional form with sweeping copper-green hipped roofs and deep eaves, round courts (the Chowaden with its 160 m balcony faces the east court where the public gathers at New Year). Set in the woods of the western palace grounds.

landmarks.name: Fujimi-yagura
landmarks.desc: The Fujimi-yagura of Edo Castle (1659): a three-tier white-plastered keep with grey tiled roofs and curved gables, 16 m, on a 15 m rampart of fitted stone at the south corner of the Honmaru.

landmarks.name: Ote-mon gate
landmarks.desc: The Ote-mon, the main gate of Edo Castle and the entrance to the East Gardens: a square masugata court of stone walls entered by a small Korai-mon and turned through the big two-storey white watari-yagura gatehouse, the bridge over the moat in front.

landmarks.name: Kabuki-za
landmarks.desc: The Kabuki-za (rebuilt 2013 by Kengo Kuma to the 1924 / 1951 design): a white Momoyama-revival theatre front on Harumi-dori with a great curved karahafu gable over the entrance, tiled hip-and-gable roofs, red lanterns and purple curtains; the plain 145 m Kabukiza Tower with its white lattice rises behind (extra.tower).

landmarks.name: Wako (Ginza 4-chome clock tower)
landmarks.desc: The 1932 Hattori clock tower (Wako / Seiko House) on the Ginza 4-chome crossing: a neo-Renaissance stone building whose facade curves round the corner, seven storeys, with the square clock tower on top that chimes the hours.

landmarks.name: Ginza Place
landmarks.desc: Ginza Place (2016) across the crossing from Wako: an eleven-storey block wrapped in a white lattice of aluminium panels like openwork basketry, with glazed showrooms at the corner.

landmarks.name: Ginza Mitsukoshi
landmarks.desc: Ginza Mitsukoshi, the department store on the east corner of the 4-chome crossing: a cream stone block with a glass-and-steel new wing, a lion statue at the door and a roof terrace.

landmarks.name: Zojo-ji (Sangedatsumon and the main hall)
landmarks.desc: Zojo-ji, the Tokugawa family temple under Tokyo Tower: the Daiden main hall (1974) with a huge sweeping grey-tiled hip-and-gable roof over white walls and red-brown timberwork, at the head of a stone court; in front on Hibiya-dori stands the Sangedatsumon (1622), a 21 m two-storey vermilion gate (extra.gate).

landmarks.name: Tsukiji Hongan-ji
landmarks.desc: Ito Chuta's 1934 Tsukiji Hongan-ji: a grey granite temple in ancient Indian style, a symmetrical front with a round-arched (chaitya) central roof bearing a lotus motif, stupa-topped bell towers at both ends, broad steps and stone beasts.

landmarks.name: Hie Shrine
landmarks.desc: Hie Shrine on its wooded hill at Nagatacho: a vermilion-and-white shrine hall and gate with green copper roofs round a gravel court, reached by stairs through the distinctive Sanno torii (a torii with a gabled peak) and a tunnel of red torii at the back.

landmarks.name: Atago Shrine
landmarks.desc: Atago Shrine on the 26 m Atago hill, the highest natural point of the old city: a small red-lacquered gate and timber shrine hall by a carp pond among camphor trees, at the top of the steep 86-step stone 'stairway to success'.

landmarks.name: Tokyo International Forum
landmarks.desc: Rafael Vinoly's 1996 Tokyo International Forum: a 60 m high, 207 m long lens-shaped Glass Hall along the railway, its roof a ribbed steel keel like a ship's hull held on two columns, and four graduated cube-shaped halls in grey granite on the west side, a tree-planted granite plaza between.

landmarks.name: Imperial Hotel
landmarks.desc: The Imperial Hotel facing Hibiya Park: the 1970 main building, a broad cross-plan seventeen-storey block in brown tile, and the 1983 31-storey tower (129 m) of bronze glass behind it.

landmarks.name: Ministry of Justice (red-brick building)
landmarks.desc: The 1895 Ministry of Justice by Ende and Bockmann: a three-storey German neo-Baroque block of red brick with white stone bands, arcaded loggias, corner pavilions and steep slate mansard roofs with dormers.

landmarks.name: Prime Minister's Office (Kantei)
landmarks.desc: The 2002 Prime Minister's Office: a low five-storey modern block of glass, steel louvres and stone set in a bamboo garden on the slope above Sanno, flat-roofed and symmetrical.

landmarks.name: Supreme Court of Japan
landmarks.desc: Okada Shinichi's 1974 Supreme Court: massive interlocking blocks of rough white Inada granite with slit windows, like a fortress, on the corner of the palace moat.

landmarks.name: National Theatre
landmarks.desc: The 1966 National Theatre: a long dark-brown precast concrete block shaped like an azekura log storehouse (after the Shosoin), with horizontal 'log' bands and a wide flat eave, facing the Hanzo moat.

landmarks.name: Bank of Japan (old building)
landmarks.desc: Tatsuno Kingo's 1896 Bank of Japan head office: a neo-Baroque stone palace round a forecourt with a columned central block under a green copper dome, the later bank buildings attached to the east.

landmarks.name: Nihonbashi Mitsukoshi
landmarks.desc: The Nihonbashi Mitsukoshi main store (1914 / 1935): a seven-storey neo-Renaissance stone block with a rusticated base, giant-order pilasters, bronze lions at the door and a roof tower.

landmarks.name: Nihonbashi
landmarks.desc: Nihonbashi, the 1911 double-arched granite bridge from which all road distances in Japan are measured, with bronze kirin and lion lamps on its parapets; the Shuto Expressway viaduct runs low over it along the river (roads: expressway).

landmarks.name: Nihonbashi Takashimaya
landmarks.desc: The 1933 Nihonbashi Takashimaya: an eight-storey department store in pale stone mixing Western classicism with Japanese brackets and rafters, a whole block long on Chuo-dori.

landmarks.name: Rainbow Bridge
landmarks.desc: The 1993 Rainbow Bridge across the north of Tokyo Bay from Shibaura to Odaiba: a white suspension bridge with two 126 m towers, a 570 m main span (798 m between anchorages) and a double deck: the Shuto Expressway on top, the bay road, the Yurikamome guideway and walkways below. The loop ramp on the Shibaura side winds the lower deck up to height.

landmarks.name: Odaiba Statue of Liberty
landmarks.desc: The Odaiba Statue of Liberty: a 12.25 m replica (1/7 scale) of verdigris-green bronze on a white stone pedestal on the Odaiba seafront deck, the Rainbow Bridge behind it.

landmarks.name: Aqua City / Decks Odaiba
landmarks.desc: Aqua City Odaiba, the long seven-storey shopping mall on the Odaiba seafront beside Fuji TV: stepped terraces and wooden boardwalk decks facing the bay, a glazed atrium.

landmarks.name: Kachidoki Bridge
landmarks.desc: The 1940 Kachidoki Bridge over the mouth of the Sumida: a double-leaf bascule centre span (now fixed) between stone machinery towers, with a grey steel tied arch on each side.

landmarks.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
landmarks.desc: The Tsukiji Outer Market: blocks of low two- and three-storey shop-houses, awnings and stalls crowding narrow lanes beside the Namiyoke shrine; the entry stands on the Tsukiji Uogashi market halls (2016) at its south edge.

landmarks.name: Toyosu Market
landmarks.desc: Toyosu Market (2018), the wholesale fish market that replaced Tsukiji: the Fish Intermediate Wholesale building, a vast pale-grey four-storey box 360 m long with a green roof lawn and ramps, on the Toyosu wharf.

landmarks.name: Hama-rikyu (Nakajima teahouse)
landmarks.desc: The Nakajima-no-ochaya in the Hama-rikyu Gardens: a low cypress-shingled teahouse on an island in the tidal pond, reached by long cypress bridges (the Otsutai-bashi), black pines round the shore.

landmarks.name: Takeshiba Passenger Ship Terminal
landmarks.desc: The Takeshiba Passenger Ship Terminal, where the Izu and Ogasawara island ships sail from: low terminal buildings round a plaza paved like a ship's deck with a tall white mast monument.

landmarks.name: Takanawa Gateway Station
landmarks.desc: Kengo Kuma's 2020 Takanawa Gateway Station: a great white folded-membrane roof like origami on steel-and-cedar frames over a glazed concourse above the tracks.

landmarks.name: Shimbashi SL Plaza (C11 steam locomotive)
landmarks.desc: The C11 292 steam locomotive (1945), black with red wheels, on a short length of track in the plaza outside Shimbashi Station's Hibiya exit: the meeting place of the salarymen's quarter.

landmarks.name: GINZA SIX
landmarks.desc: GINZA SIX (2017): a block-long luxury mall on Chuo-dori with six tall flagship fronts under a continuous stainless-steel 'eave', offices above and a roof garden.

ring.title: TOKYO HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP
ring.note: Title Match ring at Hibiya Park, at about 35.6710, 139.7547: the lawns, flower beds and bandstand of Tokyo's first Western-style park and the edge of the Kasumigaseki ministry blocks beside it; the level leaves out the blocks inside venueBox in that mode. Kokyo Gaien (the palace plaza) was the first choice but has only 77 u of dry ground between the Nijubashi and Babasaki moats, short of the 92 u mat. The palace moats and Nijubashi lie to the north, the Imperial Hotel, Tokyo Midtown Hibiya and the Ginza side to the east, the ministries, the Diet and Toranomon's towers to the west, the Shiodome wall to the south-east. venueBox [minX, minZ, maxX, maxZ] = the Chicago venue x -58..+48, z -78..+78 with both grandstands; runwayBox = the entrance runway and gate (x +48..+73); east / west = 0 (nothing pulled in). No landmark centre lies within 46 u on both axes; the box is dry: filledPonds lists the park's ornamental ponds inside the box, which are left out of water (the ground there is plain park). clearToBuildings = distance from the centre to the first building of 25 m or more in each direction. tallInVenueBox lists generic buildings of 30 m or more whose footprints fall in the box (not built in that mode); freewayInVenueBox = length (u) of elevated expressway inside the box.
